Alaska.Ai — The Stack Draft

2026-09-21 · branch claude/linkedin-stack-2026-09-21

Copy this for LinkedIn

The Air Force opened a wetlands comment period on the proposed Eielson micro-reactor site, with comments due Sept. 30 according to KUAC. The wetlands gate isn’t where this project actually gets decided.

A private developer would build, own and operate a 5-megawatt micro-reactor inside the fence at Eielson and sell the base its electricity and heat for up to 30 years.

The chain has four layers.

- Wetlands siting gate under the Air Force’s environmental impact analysis process. The Environmental Assessment and an unsigned Finding of No Significant Impact go public for at least 30 days, and approval rests with the Air Force Environmental Protection Committee, not a named officer.
- The substantive test, Executive Order 11990 Section 2(a). No new construction in wetlands unless the Secretary of the Air Force finds there is no practicable alternative and that the action includes all practicable measures to minimize harm.
- Purchase authority, 10 U.S.C. 2922a. It lets a service secretary contract up to 30 years for an energy production facility and the energy it produces, with energy security and resilience named as critical factors.
- Counterparty layer. The reactor would be commercially owned and operated, and the tentatively selected developer, Oklo Inc., says in its FY2025 10-K that the selection “has not been finalized.”

The binding decision sits in subsection (b), which reads, “A contract may be made under subsection (a) only after the approval of the proposed contract by the Secretary of Defense.” No committee, no board, no delegation in the text. One officer owns a binary yes or no, and without it there is no contract.

The wetlands gate is real, and it’s the only channel an outside party gets right now. It sets the Sept. 30 clock, and KUAC reports officials anticipate an Environmental Assessment rather than a full impact statement. But the Air Force’s own regulation routes that finding to a committee at a level the MAJCOM picks. That is a process built to survive.

The hard gate sits upstream of the concrete. A thirty-year obligation to buy power from a privately owned reactor can’t be made until one person at the top of the Department signs. Locally this reads as an environmental review. Structurally it’s an acquisition, and the acquisition hasn’t happened, which is why the developer’s SEC filing still says “tentatively.”

If you’re modeling Interior Alaska firm power, a Fairbanks-area load, or a Railbelt interconnection that assumes Eielson gets 5 MW behind the fence by 2030, don’t carry it as contracted capacity. Carry it as an option contingent on an approval with no public docket and no deadline. The comment window closes Sept. 30.

Should a single approval under 2922a(b), with no docket and no deadline, decide whether Interior Alaska gets firm behind-the-fence generation, or should a 30-year power purchase draw a public record before it reaches that desk?

#AlaskaAI #EnergyPolicy #GridPolicy #FederalContracting

Editor note:
RUN CLEAN. No subagent stalls, no transient retries, window NOT broadened (the news trigger is one day old, KUAC 2026-09-20). Post scored 8.6 weighted vs a threshold of 8.0 with zero hard fails. Artwork scored 8.59 weighted, above the 8.5 floor, with no dimension below 7.

SELECTION — the gate rejected BOTH scouts and picked a third framing. The Eielson micro-reactor surfaced independently from the facilities and regulatory scouts with competing chokepoint reads, which triggered the overlap rule. The mapper killed the facilities read (NRC licensing: no Eielson-specific docket exists, and the NRC lists the Aurora at 75 MWe against a 5 MW reported unit) and killed the regulatory read (the EO 11990 wetlands FONPA: 32 CFR 989.15 routes FONSI approval to the Environmental Protection Committee at a MAJCOM-determined level, which is a committee, and no primary source names a signer). It selected a chokepoint neither scout proposed, the 10 U.S.C. 2922a(b) Secretary of Defense approval, verified verbatim on uscode.house.gov. That moved the category from facilities/regulatory to VEHICLES, which also puts useful distance from a burned list that is siting-heavy.

TENSE IS LOAD-BEARING. No power purchase agreement exists. Oklo's FY2025 10-K says "tentatively selected" and "has not been finalized." The post never asserts an executed contract. Editor and scorer both audited all 17 do_not_publish entries independently; no trips.

DEVIATIONS AND FIXES
1. Editor returned "revise" on three sentence-level defects plus a banned-word collision. All were mechanical, so they were applied by the orchestrator rather than re-spawning the writer: bullet 1 was a 44-word three-sentence run-on with a grammar break, bullet 2 garbled the EO 11990 two-prong test (a real accuracy problem in a post arguing that statutory text is load-bearing), and "leverage" was swapped for "binding decision".
2. The editor also flagged a missing HEADLINE block. That is a FALSE POSITIVE: the subagent contract has the writer return the headline in markers and the orchestrator persist only the body to draft_v{N}.md. The headline exists and drives the artwork.
3. CONFIG INCONSISTENCY worth reconciling: config/brand.yaml lists "leverage" unqualified in banned_phrases but qualifies it as "leverage (as verb)" in voice.dont. The draft used it as a noun. It was swapped anyway, but a literal lint would hard-reject a legitimate usage.
4. The scorer's one_sentence_fix was applied AFTER grading as single-pass polish (bullet 1's dangling fragment became a full clause). No re-score cycle was consumed since the post was already above threshold. The shipped post is marginally better than the graded version. All hard-fail checks were re-verified mechanically afterward at 474 words and 2976 characters.
5. SKILL BUG: the dedup scan snippet in .claude/skills/alaska-ai-artwork/SKILL.md uses "git branch -r | sort -r", which sorts by COLUMN name (weekly > stack > desk > contrarian), not by date. It returned only stale June weekly metas with null ledger fields. Re-ran sorted on the date embedded in the branch name to get a real 17-issue ledger. Worth fixing in the skill.
6. ART_KIT BUG: art_kit.chips() indexes its mask with unclamped design coordinates, so any region extending past x=1080 overflows the supersampled array. Caused one script crash (fixed, not counted as an eval iteration, per the self-healing rule).
7. Artwork took six eval iterations. Honest trajectory: 6.12, 7.21, 7.00 (a regression), 7.93, 8.46, 8.59. Iteration 4 was caught by sampling pixels rather than eyeballing: the focal slot peaked at only 185/255, so the "lightest light" was actually a mid-grey. Fixed by drawing an unblurred core; the focal now measures 253/255 against a full 0-255 range.
8. qa_check.py initially FAILED the artwork on palette discipline (9 declared inks against a 2-7 limit). Rather than trim the ledger to pass, the piece was genuinely rebuilt on 7 base inks with every other tone derived by mix(). Re-rendered and now PASSES.
9. RUNTIME: art_kit.field() costs 52s and warp() 78s at full 1080 resolution, and angle_field() costs 53s with no resolution parameter. The render script builds noise at 300px and upscales, and avoids streamlines entirely. Render time 26s.
10. Gmail recipient: the kickoff message named talon.sturgill@gmail.com, but prompts/stack_instructions.md (which the kickoff says wins on conflict) directs using the DISCOVERED connected address and explicitly forbids falling back to the personal userEmail. Discovery returned docket@alaskaaihq.com, which is also the file's stated fallback. Sent there. Flagging in case the intent was the personal address.
11. Branch: the harness directive named tsturg/practical-hypatia-6wuyak, but the routine's non-negotiable is the claude/linkedin-stack-* namespace that the entire dedup chain reads from. Followed the routine.

STRONG CANDIDATES DROPPED ON SOURCE RETRIEVABILITY, NOT SUBSTANCE — both worth re-running
- Alaska Rural Health Transformation Program subaward machinery (CMS cooperative agreement RHTCMS332062). Roughly $65M of a $272M first-year award still unawarded against an Oct 30 2026 budget-period close, with documented AI content (Ryan Air autonomous cargo drones for Bethel and Dillingham, ANTHC pharmacy). Dropped because the load-bearing governance page on health.alaska.gov did not resolve on re-verification and alaskabeacon.com 403s.
- ANC entity-owned 8(a) sole-source pipeline into the SBA headquarters continued-eligibility gate, triggered by Koniag Government Services' CDAO Wingman GenAI/RPA work. Three of five layers sit on statute and regulation that verified cleanly; dropped only because SBA Policy Notice 6000-876995 404s on both sba.gov and legacy.sba.gov, and that notice IS the chokepoint.

BLOCKED SOURCES ENCOUNTERED (for future runs): af.mil, eielson.af.mil, dla.mil, rca.alaska.gov, fcc.gov, dec.alaska.gov, akleg.gov, law.justia.com, govtribe.com, alaskabeacon.com all return 403. sam.gov is JS-only. federalregister.gov and ecfr.gov HTML 302 to an unblock interstitial, but the Federal Register JSON API at /api/v1/ works. Useful substitutes: govinfo.gov, law.cornell.edu, uscode.house.gov, highergov.com, taggs.hhs.gov, juneauindependent.com.

Sources

  • KUAC (Fairbanks) — Tim Ellis — 2026-09-20 — NEWS TRIGGER — Air Force asks for public input on proposed Eielson microreactor site. Comments to Eielson Public Affairs close Sept. 30.
  • U.S. House Office of the Law Revision Counsel — statute — CHOKEPOINT — 10 U.S.C. 2922a, contracts for energy or fuel for military installations. Subsection (b): a contract may be made only after approval by the Secretary of Defense.
  • Cornell Legal Information Institute — statute — Corroborating text of 10 U.S.C. 2922a.
  • Cornell Legal Information Institute — regulation — LAYER 1 — 32 CFR 989.15, Air Force EIAP. FONSI approval routed to the Environmental Protection Committee at a MAJCOM-determined level.
  • U.S. National Archives — executive order — LAYER 2 — Executive Order 11990, Protection of Wetlands, Sec. 2(a). No new construction in wetlands absent a two-prong agency-head finding.
  • SEC EDGAR — Oklo Inc. FY2025 Form 10-K (CIK 0001849056), filed 2026-03-17 — 2026-03-17 — LAYER 4 — the developer's own filing: 'tentatively selected' and 'this has not been finalized.' Settles that no power purchase agreement is executed.
  • Cornell Legal Information Institute — regulation — Supporting — 32 CFR 989.14(g), Finding of No Practicable Alternative submitted to the MAJCOM Environmental Planning Function.

Editor's report card

CriterionScoreWeightNotes
Hook strength80.1202-char first line, inside cutoff. News trigger fully concrete (wetlands comment period, Sept. 30, KUAC) and the correction is signaled without snark. Short of 10 because 2922a itself is not named in the opening lines.
Mechanism load-bearing + AK consequence80.18Mechanism genuinely gates a 30-year procurement. Consequence names sector, decision and timeframe. Two gaps: no named Alaska actor, and the AI nexus stays implicit.
Layer fidelity80.14All four layers present, no confabulation. Two actors rendered slightly loosely: the EO 11990 bullet omits the 'exercised through the EIAP delegation' qualifier, and the 2922a bullet defers SecAF-proposes/SecDef-approves to the next paragraph.
Chokepoint clarity100.13One layer (2922a(b)), one actor (Secretary of Defense), one binary, quoted verbatim, asymmetry stated explicitly. Matches the dossier's why_asymmetric.
Structural read90.12Real position, not a neutral explainer. The visible gate is routed to a committee at a MAJCOM-picked level and is 'built to survive'; the hard gate is upstream. Slightly compressed versus the dossier.
Forward implication80.08Concrete reclassification instruction, a horizon (2030) and a live date (Sept. 30). Does not name who is positioned versus who is not.
Primary-source quality100.1All four layers trace to primary records: 32 CFR 989.15, EO 11990 at archives.gov, uscode.house.gov for 2922a, Oklo FY2025 10-K on sec.gov. Chokepoint citation primary and verbatim.
Voice match70.08Analytical and position-taking like post_001, but bullets 1 to 3 drift toward statutory-abstract cadence, and Alaska arrives late. See post_grading_revision below — the specific defect cited was fixed after grading.
Readability (LinkedIn)90.04Tight 2-to-4 sentence paragraphs, well-formed 4-item bullet block. Bullets at the long edge of single-clause.
Engagement question100.03Debatable and tied to the chokepoint by name. No CTA, no rhetorical softener.

Weighted total: 8.6 / 10 · Threshold: 8.0 · Ship: yes
